content: Monogenic diabetes is caused by mutations in specific genes that directly influence the production and secretion of insulin. These genetic mutations are typically inherited in one of three patterns: autosomal dominant (AD), autosomal recessive (AR), or X-linked inheritance. The genes associated with monogenic diabetes include those linked to maturity-onset diabetes of the young (MODY) and neonatal diabetes. Each gene is associated with distinct clinical features that help in the diagnosis and classification of the condition.
